A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PartCo research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCD benchmark results, component ablations, alternative label-construction experiments, and unknown-category estimation experiments in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds CLIP evaluations, annotated-part validation, foreground-only controls, computational measurements, and per-class success and failure results.

M1.justification: The proposed PCA/k-means label construction, first- and second-order priors, part-feature pooling, projection head, correspondence losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Third-order labels are investigated as an ablation; the additional backbone and host-method experiments do not revise the main algorithm.

E1.justification: All eight image datasets are retained, including Oxford-Pet and Herbarium19 from v1's appendix. The limited expansion is an auxiliary evaluation of semantic part correspondence against CUB's visible annotated parts in v2 Table F. CLIP and additional host methods change model configurations rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 substantially expand the evaluated comparator set, adding methods including APL, PartGCD, DebGCD, SEAL, RLCD, and HypCD variants. Appendix Table D introduces CLIP comparisons with TextGCD, GET, CLIP-GCD, and CPT. Oxford-Pet and Herbarium19 comparisons also add FlipClass and SelEx, beyond v1's SimGCD comparison.

E3.justification: Existing dataset splits, category ACC evaluation, and stated core training settings remain unchanged. New experimental protocols include CLIP ViT-B/16 image-encoder evaluation, additional host-model configurations, a reported balancing-factor sweep over 0, 0.1, 0.35, 0.7, and 1.0, Hungarian matching against visible CUB part annotations before downsampling, and foreground-only training controls.

E4.justification: v2 adds balancing-factor sensitivity, quantitative part-label validation, third-order over-fragmentation analysis, a foreground-only control testing whether background suppression explains the gains, computational overhead analysis, and per-class success/failure studies. Existing projection-dimension, unsupervised-loss, SD-DINOv2, and unknown-category analyses are retained. The implicit/explicit SPTNet analysis moves from v1 Table 4 to appendix Table E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing PartCo-SimGCD and PartCo-SelEx scores in Tables 1 and 2 are retained, while extensive results are added. New CLIP average ACC is 65.3 for SimGCD versus 70.5 for PartCo-SimGCD; part-label matching reports 80.8 and 77.5 for first- and second-order labels. Added Hyp-SelEx ranks above PartCo-SelEx on SSB average ACC, 86.0 versus 85.5. Newly reported SPTNet Stanford-Cars ACC is inconsistent: 72.3 in Table 1 versus 72.5 in Table E.

T1.justification: The formal problem assumptions, PCA and clustering definitions, and loss equations are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added. The new part-matching evaluation is empirical, and moving category ACC from a numbered equation to inline text does not change its definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the claim from achieving or setting the state of the art to outperforming most existing methods. The central contribution remains an explicit part-correspondence prior that improves existing GCD methods without substantial architectural changes.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning transfer beyond DINO, benefits beyond background suppression, and degradation from excessive part fragmentation. New failure analysis identifies ambiguous local appearance, informative global shape, and age-related variation. Limitations now discuss frozen PCA construction and patch-grid resolution, while CNN incompatibility is softened to reduced direct applicability. v1's detailed broader-impact discussion is replaced by a generic impact statement.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents baseline and PartCo training times, peak training memory of 8.6 versus 12.0 GB, and computational costs of 54.1 versus 62.6 GFLOPs in Table B. It specifies the CLIP ViT-B/16 image-only configuration. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, preprocessing information, label-construction timings, and project-page access remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The comparison literature expands substantially, and positioning becomes more specific. Section 5 distinguishes PartCo's training-only correspondence supervision from APL's aggregated part representation and PartGCD's adaptive decomposition and regularization. Section 4.2 contrasts PartCo with HypCD's hyperbolic embeddings. Additional references support CLIP comparisons and proposed object-centric and feature-upsampling directions.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose and the main section sequence are retained. Targeted revisions affect claims, results discussion, related work, and conclusions. The supplement gains an overview and reorganized subsections; the implicit/explicit analysis moves there, and the broader-impact section is replaced by a main-text impact statement.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Tables 1 and 2 expand and gain venue columns, Figure 6 is redesigned around four host methods, and existing diagrams and plots are rearranged. New tables and figures display compute costs, CLIP results, part validation, third-order labels, controls, and failure cases; retained appendix visualizations are enlarged and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps: Tables F and I directly assess part semantics and isolate background suppression, Table D tests transfer beyond DINO, and new compute and failure analyses clarify practical costs and boundaries. Expanded comparisons also motivate more defensible performance claims. These substantially strengthen the evidence for PartCo. The new balancing-factor description conflicts with Equation 8, SPTNet scores disagree between Tables 1 and E, and impact discussion is reduced, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the added controlled validation.
